subject.title: fix: fail closed on stale lock recovery

question: Should fs-safe intentionally disable the shipped `remove-if-unchanged` stale-lock recovery behavior now, even though existing opt-in callers will begin receiving `file_lock_stale` during recovery?
rationale: The source-level race is real, but the fix changes a public runtime option and callback contract, so automation should not choose the security-versus-compatibility policy for maintainers.

options.title: Ship fail-closed with upgrade approval
options.body: Keep the hardening direction, but require maintainer-visible compatibility approval, real runtime proof, and release-note handling before merge.

options.title: Preserve legacy behavior until a breaking path
options.body: Keep the current recovery behavior for now and introduce fail-closed-only behavior through a breaking release or explicit strict mode, accepting that the unlink race remains for opt-in callers.

options.title: Pause for a narrower recovery design
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers decide whether a different externally-authorized recovery API is needed instead of silently ignoring the legacy callback.

recommendation.title: Ship fail-closed with upgrade approval
recommendation.body: Keep the hardening direction, but require maintainer-visible compatibility approval, real runtime proof, and release-note handling before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The same person introduced and recently maintained the sidecar lock recovery behavior in the relevant history.
